Hello! This is Andrew Ferraiuolo of Google DeepMind. My team is potentialy interested in using Comparator: https://github.com/leanprover/comparator as a way of checking if proofs are genuine ones. Previously we used SafeVerify: https://github.com/GasStationManager/SafeVerify for this task.

Does Comparator (or will it) support legitimate uses of bv_decide? This might be tricky since it seems under the hood bv_decide introduces some new definitions to represent SAT certificates (or something roughly like this). SafeVerify does not support permitting bv_decide.

If this can be supported it would be really valuable for a project where bit vector reasoning comes up often!
CC @Sebastian Ullrich since it looks like you are a contributor to this project and we met once at the Lean meetup organized by Jonathan at Google in Seattle :)

Hey, I'm the author of both of these. We do currently not have a plan for the official comparator to support native_decide based proves (such as the one that bv_decide performs). The reason being that there is indeed no way at all for comparator to know whether the axioms that bv_decide introduces are legit or not. This is because they are justified by executing a piece of native code and then just introduced as axioms. So a check that just looks at the axiom and says "yup, this looks like an axiom bv_decide would add" is not enough, anyone can add such an axiom to "prove" that any SAT formula is UNSAT.

We could re-recheck the computation ourselves. However, there is an issue here: the certificate and the BitVec formula that are fed into the verification function have executable code that is controlled by the party that produced the axiom. Thus, this executable code doesn't really have to be in any relation to the Expr values that we see on the logic side and can lead us astray again. In principle, we can introduce a check that tries to check that the expressions "look like ones that bv_decide would generate" and then code-gen for these expressions but this can of course break with any change that we make to bv_decide itself.
Thanks for your speedy reply and considering this. It does sound challenging to support.
We've started using comparator at Cryspen as well. Support for bv_decide would be greatly appreciated.
